articles.title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.00166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. Early-stopping methods aim to stop once enough reasoning is available to answer. Evaluating these methods requires accounting for the cost of deciding when to stop and the reliability of the resulting answer. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol. We introduce Target-Integrate

articles.title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.00387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

articles.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
articles.summary: A surprising discovery suggests that rejuvenating the liver could help protect against Alzheimer’s disease and heart disease. USC researchers found that an experimental drug restored aging liver cells in rats, cutting levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half and bringing bad cholesterol down to youthful levels. The treatment also revived a previously unknown communication system that helps liver cells remove harmful substances from the bloodstream.

articles.title: Voters vastly underestimate the open-mindedness of their political rivals
articles.summary: People widely assume their political opponents are completely closed off to opposing viewpoints. A new study shows that correcting this misperception makes individuals much more willing to engage in conversation across party lines.

articles.title: Scientists uncover how a tiny reflection of light helps us navigate the social world
articles.summary: When assessing where another person is looking, human beings use a variety of visual cues. A new study shows that the tiny reflections of light bouncing off the surface of the eye help us accurately track gaze direction.

articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex?
